body.statement:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\), so \(\kappa=\lambda\),
\(B^4\ge(Sd)^2\), and fix the class constants.  For every deterministic
exact design \(X=(X_{st})\), every interior reference path \(z_0\), and
every \(c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}\), consider
the deterministic experiment \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) in
\texttt{def:fixed-design-induced-experiment}.  Its nearest-design estimator
satisfies
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \left[\{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2\right]
 \le
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \left[\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2\right]
 \le C\left\{\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
          \vee D_X(z_0)^2\vee N^{-\lambda}\right\}.
\]
If \(\delta_0<1/2\), the last display is at most
\(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)\).  If in addition
\(B^4>(Sd)^2\), then
\[
 cR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)
 \le
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \left[\{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2\right].
\]
Neither bound uses a lower local-modulus condition.

For every fixed admissible \(z_0\) and every
\(\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), the conditional law under
\(\mathbb K_\xi\) given the exact design, with its labels, belongs to
\(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) for \(\mathbb K_\xi\)-almost every design,
and \(\theta_{\mathfrak E}=\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\).  Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \left[\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}
 -\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2\mid(X_{st})\right]
 \le C\left\{\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
          \vee D_X(z_0)^2\vee N^{-\lambda}\right\}
\]
for almost every design; under \(\delta_0<1/2\), its right side is at most
\(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\).  If every cohort design contains \(z_{0s}\)
exactly, the displayed risk is at most
\(C\{\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\vee N^{-\lambda}\}\), and
\(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le C\{\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\vee N^{-\lambda}\}\).
If instead \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every cohort, then
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \left[\{\widehat\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2
 \mid(X_{st})\right]\le CR_D,
 \qquad R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D.
\]
No converse in terms of \(R_D\) is asserted.

For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), its labelled observed regular
conditional kernel belongs to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) for
almost every admissible \(z_0\) under the marginal law of the query, and
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau(z_0)\) there by
\texttt{lem:causal-identification}.  Hence all preceding conditional upper
bounds transfer to \(P\) at those query values and at
\(P(\cdot\mid z_0)\)-almost every exact design; no conditional version at a
null query is selected.
body.justification: The theorem constructs the bounded replicated-response and full-covariance donor product experiment, gives an explicit nearest-site rule, and bridges first to named fixed-query kernels and then almost everywhere to causal panel laws.
body.gap: Donoho's known Gaussian convex experiment and Akhavan et al.'s strongly convex estimated-minimizer problem do not supply this bounded product experiment, external full-covariance query, nearest-site geometry, or almost-everywhere causal bridge.
body.consumer: The marginal theorem combines its conditional upper mechanism with uniform fixed-query occupancy and explicit global witnesses.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(q=Sd\) and
\[
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad D_X=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda.          \tag{1}
\]
We first work in the deterministic experiment
\(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\).  Fix
\(\xi=(\mathbb Q_\xi;\mu,f,z)\).  Conditional on the donor sample, define
\[
 U_{si}=E_{si}-\mu_s-K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}
 \{Q_{s,t_{s\ell},i}-f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})\}.                       \tag{2}
\]
The donor sample is independent of all unit histories, and the histories are
independent across \((s,i)\).  Thus (2) is conditionally centered and
independent across \((s,i)\).  Boundedness gives \(|U_{si}|\le4B\), whence
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\!\left(
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}U_{si}
 \mathrel{\Big|}(Z_j)_j\right)\le16B^2A.                            \tag{3}
\]

Let \(t_s^0\) be the smallest nearest design index to \(z_{0s}\).  By the
definition of \(t_{s\ell}\),
\[
 \|X_{s,t_{s\ell}}-z_s\|_2
 \le\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})+\|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2
      +2\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2.                           \tag{4}
\]
Since \(0<\lambda\le1\), powers of order \(\lambda\) are subadditive.
Holder continuity and (4) yield
\[
 |f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})-f_s(z_s)|
 \le C\{\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda+
 \|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda+
 \|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2^\lambda\}.                      \tag{5}
\]
Projection onto the cube is nonexpansive, each balanced fold has size at
least \(N/3\), and \(\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)\le qC_\Sigma\), so
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\|\widetilde z_\ell-z\|_2^2
 \le\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)}{|I_\ell|}
 \le\frac{3qC_\Sigma}{N}.                                        \tag{6}
\]
The experiment also imposes \(\|z-z_0\|_2^2\le C_\Sigma/N\).
Expanding \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\)
into the centered sum (3) and the approximation terms (5), then using Jensen
in (6), proves
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2
 \le C\{A+D_X^2+N^{-\lambda}\}
 .                                                                \tag{7}
\]
Measurability of the nearest-design rule proves the first minimax inequality.
When \(\delta_0<1/2\),
\texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} makes the right side of
(7) at most \(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\).

For the lower bound, first note the following elementary consequence of
total variation.  If \(P_0,P_1\) have targets separated by \(\Delta\) and
\(\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le1-\eta\), then, for
\(A_0=\{|\widetilde\theta-\theta_0|<\Delta/2\}\),
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v(\widetilde\theta-\theta_v)^2
 \ge\frac{\Delta^2}{8}\{P_0(A_0^c)+P_1(A_0)\}
 \ge\frac{\eta\Delta^2}{8}.                                     \tag{8}
\]
The first inequality follows because on \(A_0\) the error under law one is
at least \(\Delta/2\), and on its complement the error under law zero is at
least \(\Delta/2\); the second is the variational definition of total
variation.

For the treated-mean channel, keep responses and donors fixed and, under
\(v\in\{-1,1\}\), take independent \(E_{si}\in\{-b,b\}\), where
\(0<b<B\), with
\[
 \Pr_v(E_{si}=b)=\frac12+v\varepsilon_s,
 \qquad \varepsilon_s=\frac{\gamma\pi_s}{bn_s\sqrt A}.             \tag{9}
\]
Since \(A\ge\pi_s^2/n_s\), sufficiently small fixed \(\gamma\) makes all
probabilities lie in \([1/4,3/4]\).  The target separation is
\(4\gamma\sqrt A\).  Their Hellinger affinity is
\[
 \prod_{s=1}^{S}(1-4\varepsilon_s^2)^{n_s/2}
 \ge\exp(-C\gamma^2/b^2)>0,                                      \tag{10}
\]
because \(\sum_sn_s\varepsilon_s^2=\gamma^2/b^2\).  The
Cauchy--Schwarz bound (7) in the proof of
\texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} makes total variation uniformly
smaller than one.  Equation (8) gives risk at least \(cA\).

For the fixed-design channel set
\[
 q_s(x)=a_0\min_{1\le t\le T}\|x-X_{st}\|_2^\lambda,
\]
with \(a_0>0\) small in terms of \(B,L,d\), and take
\(f_s=q_s/2\), \(g_s=-q_s/2\).  The argument (6)--(8) of
\texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} shows that these
surfaces lie in the class and agree at every design site.  Deterministic zero
responses, identical event laws, and identical donors therefore give
identical observations while the targets differ by \(a_0D_X\).  Equation
(8) yields risk at least \(cD_X^2\).

For the donor channel apply \texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} under
the strict interior and moment slack, with any fixed \(\eta\in(0,1)\).  Its
one-coordinate displacement lies in a cohort \(s_0\), say in coordinate
\(k\).  Under both laws use
\[
 f_{s_0}(x)=a_1|x_k-z_{0,s_0k}|^\lambda,
 \qquad f_s(x)=0\quad(s\ne s_0),                                  \tag{11}
\]
with \(a_1\) small enough for the Holder and boundedness restrictions.  Keep
the response and event laws identical.  The product total variation is at
most \(1-\eta\), whereas the target separation is at least
\(cN^{-\lambda/2}\).  Equation (8) yields risk at least
\(cN^{-\lambda}\).  Maximizing the three lower bounds and invoking (11) of
\texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} proves the deterministic
lower bound.

We next establish the fixed-query-kernel bridge.  Fix admissible \(z_0\) and
\(\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Let \(\mathcal X\) denote the
exact-design sigma-field, \(\mathcal H\) all unit histories, and
\(\mathcal Z\) the donor sigma-field.  By the definition of the fixed-query
class, \(\mathcal Z\) is independent of \(\mathcal X\vee\mathcal H\), and
the unit histories are conditionally independent across \((s,i)\) given
\(\mathcal X\).  The two centering equalities, boundedness, and the donor
moment and covariance restrictions therefore show that, for
\(\mathbb K_\xi\)-almost every \(X\), the conditional observed law with its
labels is in \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\), at its central point
\(z=z_0\).  Its statistical target is
\[
 \theta_{\mathfrak E}
 =\sum_s\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0).                                 \tag{12}
\]
Applying (7) conditionally proves the fixed-query nearest-design bound; under
\(\delta_0<1/2\), the geometry lemma converts it to the
\(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\) bound.

If each design contains \(z_{0s}\), then \(D_X=0\), and the exact-site
claim follows from the geometry lemma.  Suppose instead
\(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every \(s\).  Then
\((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\) is feasible in every foldwise anchor search, so
certificate optimality gives
\[
\begin{split}
 &C_H\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda
 +C_V(Tn_s\widehat h_{s\ell}^d)^{-1/2}\\
 &\quad\le C_H\|z_{0s}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H(h_s^\star)^\lambda
 +C_V\{Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d\}^{-1/2}.
\end{split}                                                         \tag{13}
\]
The floor makes the last term no larger than \((h_s^\star)^\lambda\).
Since \(r=0\), the fit weights are nonnegative and sum to one.  Holder
continuity bounds approximation bias by the first two terms on the left of
(13); whole-history conditional independence bounds variance by \(CA\).
Donor unbiasedness, (6) at \(z=z_0\), Jensen's inequality, and (13) imply
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [\{\widehat\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2\mid\mathcal X]
 \le CR_D.                                                        \tag{14}
\]
The final assertion of the geometry lemma gives
\(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D\).

Finally fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).  By the two corrected
query-conditional assumptions and the remaining conditional member
properties, there is a common full-marginal-measure set of admissible query
values on which its labelled regular conditional kernel satisfies every
condition in \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}; hence it belongs to
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Assumption
\texttt{ass:donor-training-separation} is crucial here: it factors donors
from the entire joint panel, so the factorization remains valid after
conditioning on \(\mathcal X\).  Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification}
gives \(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau(z_0)\) on the same set.  Equations
(12)--(14) therefore transfer to the causal conditional kernel for almost
every query and almost every exact design.  This argument never chooses a
regular conditional version on a query-null set.
